text:
ana: heads-up — p95 +~12ms on the small-route (/chat/compact) after yesterday's kernel switchover. looks like microbatch formation time + KV-miss amplification. attaching quick notes and a short repro

bench-bot: nightly-profile uploaded -> s3://redwood-profiles/3032101111/compact-pprof.pb.gz :mag:

li: i saw the same on canary. KV hit-rate for seq_len<=64 dropped ~2.8%. CPU-side kernel launch overhead for fused-attn-v2 seems higher for tiny batches. this amplifies when batching heuristics create many 1-2 request microbatches.

mike: does anyone have the batch-formation histograms? my guess: min_batch_tokens is too aggressive and continuous-batcher is forming small microbatches to hit latency targets, but kernel change increases per-batch fixed cost.

priya: adding the histograms from staging (trimmed):
```
batch_size_hist: {1: 32%, 2: 26%, 3: 18%, 4+: 24%}
mean_tokens_per_batch: 58
kv_hit_by_seq: {<=64: 67%, >64: 88%}
```
The combo (many tiny batches + lower KV hit) explains p95.

sam: proposal: move to p95-stratified token budgets by route/tier. quick sketch:
```yaml
route_rules:
  /chat/compact:
    tiers:
      free: {target_tokens: 6, min_wait_ms: 6}
      paid: {target_tokens: 14, min_wait_ms: 4}
      enterprise: {target_tokens: 26, min_wait_ms: 2}
batcher:
  continuous:
    max_microbatch_wait_ms: 15
    prefer_age_over_size: true
    min_batch_tokens: 24
```
Goal: encourage slightly larger microbatches on compact route for paid/enterprise, reduce kernel launch overhead impact while keeping p95 targets.

mike: i like that. also add a small hysteresis so we don't thrash between budgets when traffic is spiky: keep last_applied_budget for 30s per route instance.

priya: experiment plan:
- Phase A (10% traffic): apply stratified budgets to /chat/compact on one deployment pool
- Collect: p95, p99, mean_throughput, kv_hit_by_seq, batch_size_hist, cpu_gpu_kernel_time breakdown
- Phase B (50%): if p95 improves or stays within 2ms of baseline but throughput/cost improves -> widen
- Rollback: instant if p99 regresses >5% or any error spike

sam: queue-policy detail: when tokens_remaining < target_tokens, prefer oldest requests from paid/enterprise over free. pseudo: 
```
if tokens_remaining < target:
  eligible = queue.filter(route_tier in [enterprise, paid])
  serve = eligible.take_oldest(up_to=target_tokens)
else:
  serve = queue.serve_by_size_priority()
```
This reduces starvation for higher tiers and avoids tiny batches by drawing from slightly older queued requests.

li: small caveat: KV cache eviction churn caused KV-miss drop. root cause might be that fused-attn-v2 uses a slightly different KV-cache key lifetime due to kernel parallelism. i'm instrumenting KV lifetimes and will push a diff to canary.

mike: for the perf regression repro i will run two runs on staging: (A) legacy kernel + current budgets, (B) fused-attn-v2 + proposed stratified budgets. will capture pprof and the kernel timing breakdown. scheduled for 3032101170.

bench-bot: perf job scheduled: perf-3032101170 (staging, compact loadgen). ETA ~20m. artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/perf-3032101170/

priya: metrics to watch in the rollout dashboard: 
- p95 latency (route=/chat/compact)
- batch_size_histogram (buckets 1..8+)
- kv_hit_by_seq (<=64, 65-128, >128)
- kernel_launch_overhead_ms
- tokens_per_batch_mean
- cost_per_inference (GPU-ms/token)

ana: SGTM. priya/mike, coordinate on the 10% rollout and tag me when perf artifacts upload. if bench shows p95 still regressing, we fallback kernel-only on the pool and isolate to investigate KV key lifetime.

mike: will do. quick note: let's also add a debug flag to batcher to force "batch_lookahead=20ms" so we can A/B microbatch timing without changing token budgets. that helps isolate token-budget vs kernel cost.

priya: adding that to the experiment. I'll update canary config and create a tiny PR with the YAML and rollout steps.

ana: thanks — i'll ping infra to hold any unrelated deploys for the next 2h during the canary.

sam: one more: if we see improved p95 but worse cost, we can try quantized kernel fallback for free tier to keep costs down while paid keeps the higher token budgets.

mike: noted. starting the perf runs now.

bench-bot: perf artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-perf/perf-3032101170/artifacts.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

li: initial glance: fused-attn-v2 adds ~3.9ms fixed per microbatch on A100 for seq<=64. but with target_tokens bumped to 14, mean batch size rises to 3.9 and amortizes that fixed cost — p95 drops ~7ms vs no-budget-change. kv_hit recovered ~1.5%. more detailed analysis incoming.

ana: perfect. keep updates short here and paste final numbers once we have them. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
